recentItems.title: Yemen Houthis Out For Blood: Saudi Oil Sites Attacked, MBS' ARAMCO Meltdown| Riyadh Airport On Radar
recentItems.description:
Yemen's Houthi group has announced that it conducted six separate operations involving missiles and drones against Saudi Arabia, with the strikes aimed at oil facilities as well as King Khalid International Airport located in Riyadh.

Yahya Saree, the military spokesperson for the Houthis, stated that these attacks — carried out using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones — were launched as a response to what he described as Saudi aggression against Yemen.

His claims have not been independently verified.

Saree went through the operations one at a time, listing each of them in turn.

According to him, the first of these struck King Khalid International Airport, along with oil storage tanks and an Aramco distillation tower located in Riyadh, and it successfully achieved its objective.

The second operation was directed at Aramco facilities situated in Khurais, while the third one struck Pumping Station Number 8, which is located in the Dawadmi area.

He stated that the fourth operation targeted Saudi military concentrations at a National Guard camp in Najran, and that the fifth struck troop positions to the east of Al-Jawf governorate, carrying this out in three stages.

The sixth operation targeted troop concentrations east of the Raghwah and Madghal districts in Marib governorate, acting under a Saudi officer whom he named as Fares Al-Shammari, leaving a large number of dead and wounded among their ranks.

As of now, no casualty figures have been confirmed.

recentItems.title: Saudi Airstrikes Kill Over 2 Dozen Near Sanaa, Houthis Come Face-To-Face With Yemen Troops In Taiz
recentItems.description:
According to a spokesman for Yemen's Health Ministry, which is run by the Houthis, airstrikes struck homes in a village close to Sanaa, the country's capital, resulting in the deaths of at least 27 people and injuries to 36 more.

According to officials from the Houthi movement, an airstrike that struck a marketplace in southern Yemen at an earlier point resulted in the deaths of no fewer than 30 people.

Video captured in the farming village — which sits in territory controlled by the Houthis, roughly 15 kilometers to the northeast of Sanaa — revealed the debris of homes that had been demolished, with dust swirling through the air while residents took cover in the agricultural fields close by.
